Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with complaints of neck pain and low back pain with associated
muscle stiffness and limited range of motion. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported incident, and the presenting
complaints are plausible for this type of impact. Examination revealed paraspinal muscle tenderness and reduced cervical and
lumbar motion, and imaging findings clearly confirm soft tissue injury consistent with cervical and lumbar strain. No prior injury
or treatment to the same body regions is known to this provider. Care consisted of ten visits including manual therapy,
therapeutic exercise, and home stretching instruction. The treatment course followed a typical progression, with visit frequency
tapering as symptoms improved and range of motion returned toward baseline. Billed services reflect the treatment rendered,
with no repeated charges for the same service. Prognosis is good with continued home exercise and as-needed follow-up.
